I'm working with patient and examination data in PostgreSQL and trying to summarize information for each patient. My goal is to get a count of all examinations associated with each patient, and also separate counts for examinations where a specific condition (let's call it 'thrombosis') was recorded as either present (value 1) or absent (value 0).

I have records linking patients to their various examinations over time. The issue I'm running into is handling cases where the thrombosis status for a particular examination record might be missing or null. When I try to aggregate this information, my attempts seem to incorrectly filter out patients or miscount the total examinations if any of the thrombosis statuses are null. I want to make sure I get the total count of *all* examinations for every patient, regardless of the thrombosis status, alongside the specific counts for when thrombosis was explicitly recorded as 1 or 0.

For example, if a patient had 3 examinations, one with thrombosis=1, one with thrombosis=0, and one where the thrombosis status is unknown (null), I'd expect to see that patient listed with a total examination count of 3, a thrombosis count of 1, and a no-thrombosis count of 1. My current approaches don't seem to achieve this correctly; they either drop the patient or don't give the right total count.

How can I structure my query to correctly count the total number of examinations per patient, while also separately summing up the counts for examinations explicitly marked with thrombosis status 1 and status 0, ensuring patients aren't excluded just because some of their examination records have a null status for thrombosis?
issue_sql: WITH PatientExamData AS (SELECT P.ID AS PATIENTID, P.SEX, P.BIRTHDAY, E."Examination Date", E.DIAGNOSIS, E.THROMBOSIS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY P.ID ORDER BY E."Examination Date" NULLS FIRST) AS ExamRank FROM patient AS P LEFT JOIN examination AS E ON P.ID = E.ID), LatestLabResults AS (SELECT L.ID, L.PLT, L.WBC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY L.ID ORDER BY L."date" DESC NULLS LAST) AS LabRank FROM laboratory AS L WHERE L."date" <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP), PatientRiskProfile AS (SELECT PED.PATIENTID, PED.SEX, PED.BIRTHDAY, PED."Examination Date", PED.DIAGNOSIS, PED.THROMBOSIS, CASE WHEN LLR.PLT < 150 OR LLR.WBC > 11 THEN 'High' WHEN PED.THROMBOSIS IS NULL THEN 'Unknown' ELSE 'Normal' END AS RiskCategory FROM patientexamdata AS PED LEFT JOIN latestlabresults AS LLR ON PED.PATIENTID = LLR.ID AND LLR.LabRank = 1) SELECT PATIENTID, SEX, BIRTHDAY, COUNT("Examination Date") AS EXAMINATIONCOUNT, SUM(CASE WHEN THROMBOSIS = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS THROMBOSISCOUNT, SUM(CASE WHEN THROMBOSIS = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS NOTHROMBOSISCOUNT, MAX(CASE WHEN RiskCategory = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS HighRiskFlag FROM patientriskprofile WHERE RiskCategory <> 'Unknown' OR THROMBOSIS IN (0, 1) GROUP BY PATIENTID, SEX, BIRTHDAY HAVING COUNT("Examination Date") > 0 ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN THROMBOSIS = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC NULLS LAST, PATIENTID NULLS FIRST

I'm trying to combine information from patient records with their corresponding examination details in PostgreSQL. My goal is to see a list that includes all the patient's basic information alongside the results from their specific examinations, like the examination date, diagnosis, and various test results (e.g., 'aCL IgG', 'aCL IgM', 'ana').

I've attempted to link these records based on the patient identifier found in both sets of data. However, I'm finding it tricky to get the structure right. My attempts feel overly complex, and I'm not certain I'm correctly matching every examination to its patient, especially since some patients might not have any examination records. I just need a clear way to retrieve all patient details and, for those who have them, their associated examination information on the same line.

How can I structure a query to effectively pull all patient information and correctly join it with their related examination details?
issue_sql: WITH PatientExamHistory AS (SELECT p.id, p.sex, p.birthday, p.description, p."First Date", p.admission, p.diagnosis AS PatientDiagnosis, e."Examination Date", e."aCL IgG", e."aCL IgM", e.ana, e."ANA Pattern", e."aCL IgA", e.diagnosis AS ExamDiagnosis, e.kct, e.rvvt, e.lac, e.symptoms, e.thrombosis, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.id ORDER BY e."Examination Date" DESC NULLS LAST) AS ExamRank, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY p.id) AS ExamCount FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN examination AS e ON e.id = p.id LEFT JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id AND l.date = e."Examination Date" WHERE (p.sex = 'F' OR e.thrombosis = 1)), LatestLabResults AS (SELECT l.id, l.date, l.wbc, l.rbc, l.hgb, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.id ORDER BY l.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS LabRank FROM laboratory AS l) SELECT peh.*, llr.wbc, llr.rbc, llr.hgb, CASE WHEN peh.ExamCount > 1 THEN 'Multiple Exams' WHEN peh.ExamCount = 1 THEN 'Single Exam' ELSE 'No Exams' END AS ExamStatus FROM patientexamhistory AS peh LEFT JOIN latestlabresults AS llr ON llr.id = peh.id AND llr.LabRank = 1 WHERE peh.ExamRank = 1 OR peh.ExamRank IS NULL ORDER BY CASE WHEN peh.thrombosis = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END NULLS FIRST, peh.id NULLS FIRST

I have a table that links lab results to patient IDs, and includes the date the lab test was performed. When I try to query this, I often end up with multiple rows for the same patient ID, showing all their historical lab results. What I actually need is just one row per patient ID, representing their latest available lab data.

I've tried ordering the results by date, but I'm not sure how to filter it down to just the single most recent entry for each patient ID. How can I structure my query in PostgreSQL to achieve this, ensuring I only get the very last lab record for each patient?

WITH LabResults AS (
    SELECT l.id, l.date, l.got, l.gpt, l.ldh, l.alp, l.tp, l.alb, l.ua, l.un, l.cre, l."T-BIL", l."T-CHO", l.tg, l.cpk, l.glu, l.wbc, l.rbc, l.hgb, l.hct, l.plt, l.pt, l.aptt, l.fg, l."U-PRO", l.igg, l.iga, l.igm, l.crp, l.ra, l.rf, l.c3, l.c4, l.rnp, l.sm, l.sc170, l.ssa, l.ssb, l.centromea, l.dna, l."DNA-II",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.id ORDER BY l.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS LatestRank,

        WHEN l.crp IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN l.crp IN ('Positive', 'Negative') THEN 1

    LEFT JOIN patientdiagnosis AS pd ON lr.id = pd.id

query:
I'm working with patient laboratory data where each patient ID can have multiple entries corresponding to different test dates. I need to extract only the most recent set of laboratory results for each patient.

I've attempted to isolate these latest records, possibly by trying to rank them based on the date for each patient. However, I'm finding it tricky to get just the single latest entry consistently. My attempts sometimes seem to get complicated, especially when considering how to handle records where certain test results might be missing or have specific text values, leading to either incorrect records being selected or multiple records returned per patient instead of just the most recent one.

Could someone explain how I can reliably retrieve just the single, most recent complete laboratory record for every patient, based purely on the latest test date associated with their ID in PostgreSQL?
issue_sql:
WITH LabResults AS (
    SELECT l.id, l.date, l.got, l.gpt, l.ldh, l.alp, l.tp, l.alb, l.ua, l.un, l.cre, l."T-BIL", l."T-CHO", l.tg, l.cpk, l.glu, l.wbc, l.rbc, l.hgb, l.hct, l.plt, l.pt, l.aptt, l.fg, l."U-PRO", l.igg, l.iga, l.igm, l.crp, l.ra, l.rf, l.c3, l.c4, l.rnp, l.sm, l.sc170, l.ssa, l.ssb, l.centromea, l.dna, l."DNA-II",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.id ORDER BY l.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS LatestRank,
    CASE
        WHEN l.crp IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN l.crp IN ('Positive', 'Negative') THEN 1
        ELSE 2
    END AS CRPType
    FROM laboratory AS l
    INNER JOIN patient AS p ON l.id = p.id
    WHERE p.sex = 'F'
),
PatientDiagnosis AS (
    SELECT id, MAX(CASE WHEN diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS HasSLE
    FROM examination
    GROUP BY id
),
LatestLabWithRank AS (
    SELECT lr.*,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lr.id ORDER BY lr.CRPType DESC NULLS LAST, lr.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS PriorityRank
    FROM labresults AS lr
    LEFT JOIN patientdiagnosis AS pd ON lr.id = pd.id
    WHERE (lr.LatestRank = 1 OR (pd.HasSLE = 1 AND lr.LatestRank <= 3))
)
SELECT l.id, l.date, l.got, l.gpt, l.ldh, l.alp, l.tp, l.alb, l.ua, l.un, l.cre, l."T-BIL", l."T-CHO", l.tg, l.cpk, l.glu, l.wbc, l.rbc, l.hgb, l.hct, l.plt, l.pt, l.aptt, l.fg, l."U-PRO", l.igg, l.iga, l.igm, l.crp, l.ra, l.rf, l.c3, l.c4, l.rnp, l.sm, l.sc170, l.ssa, l.ssb, l.centromea, l.dna, l."DNA-II"
FROM latestlabwithrank AS l
WHERE l.PriorityRank = 1 AND (NOT l.crp IN ('Positive', 'Negative') OR l.CRPType > 0)
ORDER BY l.id NULLS FIRST

query:
I'm working with patient data and their corresponding laboratory test results. Each patient has basic information like an ID, sex, and diagnosis stored separately from their lab results, which include the date the test was performed. A patient can have many lab tests over time.

My goal is to create a summary showing each patient's ID, sex, and diagnosis, alongside the date of their *very first* laboratory test. I've tried joining the patient information with their lab records based on the patient ID, but I'm struggling to correctly isolate just the earliest test date for every unique patient. I seem to be getting more rows than expected or not the minimum date I need for each individual.

How can I structure my query to get a single row per patient containing their details and only the earliest date from their lab test history?
issue_sql: WITH PatientTestDates AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, p.Diagnosis, l.Date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY l.Date NULLS FIRST) AS RowNum FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.Date >= p."First Date" OR p."First Date" IS NULL), ExaminationDates AS (SELECT p.ID, MIN(e."Examination Date") AS earliest_exam_date FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN examination AS e ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.ID) SELECT ptd.ID, ptd.SEX, ptd.Diagnosis, CASE WHEN ptd.Date < ed.earliest_exam_date OR ed.earliest_exam_date IS NULL THEN ptd.Date ELSE ed.earliest_exam_date END AS earliest_test_date FROM patienttestdates AS ptd LEFT JOIN examinationdates AS ed ON ptd.ID = ed.ID WHERE ptd.RowNum = 1 GROUP BY ptd.ID, ptd.SEX, ptd.Diagnosis, ptd.Date, ed.earliest_exam_date
sol_sql: SELECT p.id, p.sex, p.diagnosis, MIN(l.date) AS earliest_test_date FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id GROUP BY p.id, p.sex, p.diagnosis

query:
I'm trying to create a report that lists all patients from our system along with their diagnosis and their thrombosis status. The patient information and the examination results (which contain the thrombosis status) seem to be stored separately.

My main challenge is combining this information correctly. When I tried to pull the data together, I ended up with multiple rows for some patients, which isn't what I want. I need just one row per patient. Also, some patients might not have any examination records, but I still need them included in my final list, perhaps showing a default thrombosis status like '0' in those cases.

I've tried different approaches to link the patient details with their examination results, but I keep getting these duplicate patient entries or missing patients who don't have examination data.

How can I structure my query to get a unique list of all patients, showing their ID, diagnosis, and their thrombosis status (using 0 if no examination record is available for a patient)?
issue_sql: WITH PatientThrombosisHistory AS (SELECT e.ID, e.Thrombosis, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.ID ORDER BY e."Examination Date" DESC NULLS LAST) AS RecencyRank, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY e.ID) AS ExamCount FROM examination AS e WHERE NOT e.Thrombosis IS NULL), LabResults AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PLT) AS AvgPlateletCount, MAX(CASE WHEN l.PLT < 150 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS HasLowPlatelets FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.Date >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '-1 YEAR' GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT p.ID AS PatientID, p.Diagnosis, CASE WHEN lr.HasLowPlatelets = 1 AND pth.Thrombosis IS NULL THEN 1 WHEN pth.ExamCount > 1 THEN (SELECT Thrombosis FROM examination WHERE ID = p.ID ORDER BY "Examination Date" NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) ELSE COALESCE(pth.Thrombosis, 0) END AS ThrombosisStatus, lr.AvgPlateletCount FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN patientthrombosishistory AS pth ON p.ID = pth.ID AND pth.RecencyRank = 1 LEFT JOIN labresults AS lr ON p.ID = lr.ID ORDER BY p.ID NULLS FIRST
sol_sql: SELECT p.id AS patientid, p.diagnosis, COALESCE(e.thrombosis, 0) AS thrombosisstatus FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN examination AS e ON p.id = e.id ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

query:
I'm working with patient examination data in PostgreSQL and trying to track changes in their thrombosis risk over time.

My goal is to generate a report showing, for each patient and for each month they had an examination, whether their thrombosis risk increased or decreased compared to their *previous* examination record. I only want to see the status based on the *last* examination that occurred within each specific month for that patient.

So, for a given patient and month, I need to look at the thrombosis value from their latest examination in that month and compare it to the value from their immediately preceding examination (which might have been in a previous month). Then, I want columns indicating 'Yes' or 'No' for whether the risk increased or decreased in that comparison.

I've been trying different ways to structure this, but I'm struggling to correctly compare the latest record of the month with the overall previous record for the patient, while also ensuring I only get one row per patient per month (representing the last examination of that month). I seem to be getting either too many rows or incorrect comparisons.

How can I structure a query to correctly identify the last examination record for each patient within each month and compare its thrombosis status to the patient's immediately preceding examination record to determine if the risk increased or decreased?
issue_sql:
WITH cte AS
  (SELECT id,
          "Examination Date",
          thrombosis,
          risklag = LAG(thrombosis, 1, thrombosis) OVER (PARTITION BY id
                                                         ORDER BY "Examination Date"),
          rn = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id,
                                               EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "Examination Date"),
                                               EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "Examination Date")
                                  ORDER BY "Examination Date" DESC)
   FROM examination)
SELECT id,
       startofmonth = DATE_TRUNC('month', "Examination Date")::DATE,
       increase_risk = CASE
                           WHEN risklag < thrombosis THEN 'Yes'
                           ELSE 'No'
                       END,
                       decrease_risk = CASE
                                           WHEN risklag > thrombosis THEN 'Yes'
                                           ELSE 'No'
                                       END
FROM cte
WHERE rn = 1
  AND risklag = '0'
sol_sql:
WITH cte AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        "Examination Date",
        thrombosis,
        LAG(thrombosis, 1, thrombosis) OVER (
            PARTITION BY id
            ORDER BY "Examination Date"
        ) AS risklag,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY id,
            EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "Examination Date"),
            EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "Examination Date")
            ORDER BY "Examination Date" DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM examination
)

SELECT
    id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', "Examination Date")::DATE AS startofmonth,
    CASE
        WHEN risklag < thrombosis THEN 'Yes'
        ELSE 'No'
    END AS increase_risk,
    CASE
        WHEN risklag > thrombosis THEN 'Yes'
        ELSE 'No'
    END AS decrease_risk
FROM cte
WHERE rn = 1;

My goal is to assign an indicator ('Y' or 'N') to each examination record for every patient. The very first examination for any patient should always be 'N'. For subsequent examinations, if the date is within one year of the *last relevant date* (which starts as the first examination date), it should be marked 'N', and the relevant date doesn't change. However, if an examination occurs *more* than one year after the last relevant date, it should be marked 'Y', and *this* examination's date becomes the new relevant date for checking future examinations for that same patient.

I attempted to build this sequence logic, processing examinations chronologically for each patient. I thought I could pass the 'relevant date' along from one examination to the next using a recursive method. But the results aren't right – the 'Y'/'N' indicators seem incorrect in many cases. How can I structure this analysis correctly so that each examination is properly compared against the relevant prior date (which resets after a year-long gap) to determine if it should be marked 'Y' or 'N'?

                 THEN t."Examination Date"

query:
I'm working with patient data where multiple diagnoses for a single patient are stored together in one text field, separated by commas. I need to write a query that finds all patients who have a specific diagnosis code, for instance, 'SLE'.

I've tried splitting the comma-separated string for each patient and then checking if any of the resulting diagnosis codes match 'SLE'. However, I'm concerned about how to do this safely. My current approach feels like it might be vulnerable if the search term ('SLE' in this case) were to come from user input later on, potentially allowing harmful commands to be run against the database. I'm not sure how to structure this correctly in PostgreSQL to avoid security risks.

How can I securely filter my patient records in PostgreSQL to find those that include a specific diagnosis like 'SLE' within a comma-separated text field, ensuring the query isn't susceptible to injection vulnerabilities?
issue_sql: SELECT ID, value FROM PATIENT CROSS JOIN LATERAL string_to_table(DIAGNOSIS, ',') AS s(value) WHERE DIAGNOSIS = 'SLE' || '; DROP TABLE PATIENT; --';
sol_sql: WITH params AS (SELECT 'SLE'::TEXT AS SearchDiagnosis) SELECT P.ID, s.value FROM PATIENT P CROSS JOIN LATERAL string_to_table(P.DIAGNOSIS, ',') AS s(value) CROSS JOIN params WHERE TRIM(s.value) = params.SearchDiagnosis;

I'm working with patient examination and laboratory data, and I'm trying to figure out how many unique groupings of patients exist based on their associated records.

Essentially, I want to look at each examination record, see which patient(s) are linked to it (through the lab data as well), and then count how many distinct *sets* of patients I find across all examinations.

For example, if examination 1 is associated with patients A and B, and examination 2 is also associated with patients A and B, that specific combination {A, B} should only be counted once. If examination 3 is associated with just patient C, that's a different combination {C}. I need the final total count of these unique combinations.

I've tried grouping the data in a few ways, but I'm struggling to get the logic right to identify and count only the unique sets of patients across all the examination records.

How can I structure a query to count these unique patient groupings correctly?

sol_sql:
WITH distinctCombos AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        e.id AS Laboratory_ID,
        l.id AS Patient_ID
    FROM examination e
    JOIN laboratory l ON e.id = l.id
), patientComboCount AS (
    SELECT
        e.id AS ID,
        string_agg(CAST(dc.Patient_ID AS text), ',' ORDER BY dc.Patient_ID ASC) AS patientList
    FROM examination e
    LEFT JOIN distinctCombos dc ON dc.Laboratory_ID = e.id
    GROUP BY e.id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT patientList) AS UniqueGroups
FROM patientComboCount

query:
I'm trying to figure out which experiments can be run based on the available stock of a specific material, specifically material ID 2. I have information on experiments, the materials they require, and the initial quantity of each material in inventory.

The challenge is that I need to check the experiments sequentially, ordered by their ID. If an experiment requires material 2 and there's enough stock available (considering what might have been used by *earlier* feasible experiments), then it's considered 'executable'. The quantity it uses should then be deducted from the available stock for checking the *next* experiment in the sequence.

However, if an experiment cannot be run because there isn't enough of material 2 left at that point, it should be marked as 'not executable', and importantly, its requirements should *not* impact the stock availability for any subsequent experiments.

I've been trying to figure out how to perform this kind of sequential check where the available stock effectively decreases only after a successful allocation, but I'm struggling to get the logic right for the whole sequence.

How can I generate a list that shows each experiment ID using material 2, the material ID itself (which is 2), and a status indicating whether that specific experiment is executable (let's use 1 for executable, 0 for not) based on this sequential availability check?
issue_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE ExpCTE AS (
SELECT
DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY exp_id) AS ExpRN
, exp_id
, mid
, qty
FROM
Experiment WHERE mid = 2
)
, CTE AS
(
SELECT
e.exp_id
, e.mid
, e.qty
, i.qty - e.qty AS QtyAvailable
, e.ExpRN
FROM
ExpCTE e
INNER JOIN
Inventory i ON i.mid = e.mid
WHERE
e.exp_id IN (SELECT e_sub.exp_id
FROM Experiment e_sub
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Inventory i_sub
WHERE i_sub.mid = e_sub.mid AND i_sub.qty < e_sub.qty)
ORDER BY e_sub.exp_id
LIMIT 1)
AND e.mid = 2
UNION ALL
SELECT
e.exp_id
, e.mid
, e.qty
, c.QtyAvailable - e.qty
, e.ExpRN
FROM
ExpCTE e
INNER JOIN
CTE c ON c.ExpRN + 1 = e.ExpRN AND c.mid = e.mid
WHERE
e.qty <= c.QtyAvailable
)
SELECT exp_id, mid, qty, QtyAvailable, ExpRN
FROM CTE;
sol_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
CTE_RN AS
(
SELECT
e.exp_id
,e.mid
,e.qty
,i.qty AS LimitQty
,ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY e.exp_id) AS rn
FROM
Experiment AS e
INNER JOIN Inventory AS i ON e.mid = i.mid
WHERE e.mid = 2
)
,CTE_Recursive AS
(
SELECT
r.exp_id
,r.mid
,r.qty
,r.LimitQty
,r.rn
,CASE WHEN r.qty <= r.LimitQty THEN r.qty ELSE 0 END AS ConsumedQty
,CASE WHEN r.qty <= r.LimitQty THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS Executable
FROM
CTE_RN r
WHERE
r.rn = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT
r.exp_id
,r.mid
,r.qty
,r.LimitQty
,r.rn
,CASE WHEN rec.Executable = 1 AND (r.qty + rec.ConsumedQty <= r.LimitQty)
THEN r.qty + rec.ConsumedQty
ELSE rec.ConsumedQty
END AS ConsumedQty
,CASE WHEN rec.Executable = 1 AND (r.qty + rec.ConsumedQty <= r.LimitQty)
THEN 1
ELSE 0
END AS Executable
FROM
CTE_RN r
INNER JOIN CTE_Recursive rec ON rec.rn + 1 = r.rn
)
SELECT exp_id, mid, Executable FROM CTE_Recursive ORDER BY rn;

query:
I'm working with some data where records can be linked to parent records, forming a hierarchy. Some records act as the ultimate "root" or top-level entry because they don't have a parent linked to them.

I have a specific set of starting record identifiers, for example, 657266 and 115562. For each of these starting records, I need to trace back through the parent links until I find the ultimate top-level record associated with it.

I've tried exploring ways to traverse this structure, possibly using recursion, but I'm running into trouble getting the exact output I need. My attempts seem to either return all the intermediate records in the chain back to the top, or I lose the connection showing which top-level record corresponds to which of my initial starting records (657266 or 115562).

How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL so that for each specific starting identifier (like 657266 and 115562), it returns only the identifier of its ultimate top-level ancestor record?
issue_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (
SELECT ID, ParentID
FROM LaboratoryLink
WHERE ID IN (657266, 115562)
UNION ALL
SELECT t.ID, t.ParentID
FROM LaboratoryLink t
JOIN cte c ON t.ID = c.ParentID
WHERE t.ParentID IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT *
FROM cte;
sol_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (
SELECT ID, ParentID, ID as StartID
FROM LaboratoryLink
WHERE ID IN (657266, 115562)
UNION ALL
SELECT t.ID, t.ParentID, c.StartID
FROM LaboratoryLink t
JOIN cte c ON t.ID = c.ParentID
)
SELECT c.StartID, c.ID
FROM cte c
WHERE c.ParentID IS NULL;
